messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired - PD#PD-9482 - eval-gate: safety_regression detected by nightly-evals. Affected: hosted-api v2.3.2 rollout. Trigger: toxic_score > threshold (0.05).

pagerduty-bot: Paging oncall - escalation policy 'infra-ml-safety' invoked. Primary: Elaine (SRE).

Elaine (SRE): ack. jumping in. getting quick context. who owns the rollout?

Praj (ML): @Elaine I set the canary for v2.3.2 earlier today, 10% traffic. New prompt prep changes + slightly different sampling led to eval drift on safety evals. Nightly eval gate tripped at 04:07 UTC.

Elaine (SRE): copy. do we have customer-facing failures or just eval-flagged regressions?

Praj (ML): so far only eval/regression alerts. But eval samples show more hallucination / safety tokens in certain prompts (policy: toxicity). Quick numbers: toxic_score jump from 0.03 -> 0.12 on sampled set; fail_rate 1.8% -> 9.6%.

Tony (DevEx): :eyes: any traffic spikes tied to the canary? metrics?

Elaine (SRE): monitoring - latency and error rates normal. No increased 5xx. But we should assume customer impact potential for safety-sensitive prompts.

CS Ops: flagged 1 support ticket (internal) about odd model outputs in a sandbox customer. No public complaints yet. We should proactively notify top-risk customers.

Elaine (SRE): agreed. immediate mitigation checklist: 1) Stop canary rollout (scale to 0% traffic). 2) Pin global model routing to last-known-good v2.3.1. 3) Block automatic rollouts until ML triage complete. 4) Notify CS + Legal if any customer visible issues.

Praj (ML): on it. running rollback now. command: ```redwood rollback --env=hosted --model=v2.3.2 --to=v2.3.1 --force-canary-stop```

incident-bot: Exec log: rollback job queued (job id jb-7721).

Praj (ML): rollback completed: canary scaled to 0, global pinned to v2.3.1. Canary traffic drained by 04:18 UTC.

Elaine (SRE): nice. can we run a targeted re-eval across the prompt set that tripped the gate to confirm rollback restored baseline?

Praj (ML): running quick-eval (subset of 200 prompts). ETA ~6m.

Tony (DevEx): also recommend turning on fallback routing in case any anomalous variant is reintroduced by autoscaling. Add a policy: if safety_metric > 0.06 then route to pinned-v2.3.1.

Elaine (SRE): +1. Tony, can you add that policy?

Tony (DevEx): adding policy now. snippet: ```policy safety_gate { metric: toxic_score threshold: 0.06 action: route_to model:v2.3.1 }``` applied to hosted cluster.

Praj (ML): quick-eval results: post-rollback toxic_score median 0.028, fail_rate 1.9% — back to baseline. Saved eval artifacts at s3://redwood-evals/nightly/2026-03-14/PDb-9482/.

Elaine (SRE): good. next steps: 1) create incident ticket and severity assessment. 2) assign ML triage to investigate root cause in prompt diffs & sampling. 3) CS to draft customer note in case any users saw bad outputs.

Praj (ML): creating ticket IR-2026-0314 in tracker. attaching evaluation diff + top 20 failure samples. Root suspicion: prompt pre-processing change combined with subtle sampling temperature bump.

CS Ops: drafting customer advisory template for any customers who query regressions. Will keep it internal unless we see confirmed public-facing incidents.

Oncall Roster: Elaine - can you take lead on incident for next 2 hours? then handoff to Praj for ML deep-dive?

Elaine (SRE): yes, I'll keep the incident open, run live mitigation for 2h then handoff. Logging timeline and actions in the ticket.

Praj (ML): starting deeper diff: comparing v2.3.1 vs v2.3.2 tokenizer/prompt pipeline changes. Also running targeted safety evals across customer-specific prompt classes.

Tony (DevEx): reminder to add eval gate unit tests to the CI that replicate the failing samples. We should gate PRs that touch prompt preprocessing with this test.

Elaine (SRE): agreed. immediate action item list (summary): - rollback confirmed (done) - safety fallback policy added (done) - quick-eval passed (done) - ticket IR-2026-0314 created (Praj) - CS draft prepared (CS Ops) - postmortem + remediation due EOD tomorrow.

incident-bot: Incident severity updated -> sev2 (customer-impact potential but contained).

CS Ops: will stand by to send advisory if we detect public complaints. Notifying top-10 enterprise contacts now.

Praj (ML): fyi attaching diff snippet in ticket: ```- preprocessing: trim_newlines=true  + preprocessing: trim_newlines=false``` this small change plus temp: 0.9 -> 1.0 increased tendency to produce unsafe continuations in a subset.

Elaine (SRE): excellent catch. Add remediation: revert preprocessing change in next patch and add safe-defaults to prompt templates. Action owner: Praj. ETA: 24h.

Tony (DevEx): I'm adding a CI eval gate referencing IR-2026-0314 failset. Will block future merges until green.

Elaine (SRE): handoff plan: I'll monitor for 2h, then @Praj you'll own deeper RCA and patching. Anyone else?

Praj (ML): I can pick up after 06:30 UTC.

Oncall Roster: noted. Escalation path: if safety metric > 0.06 reopens page to infra-ml-safety.

Elaine (SRE): final — creating incident channel and postmortem stub. tagging Legal & Comms for visibility. Will update once we confirm no customer-facing blast.

incident-bot: Incident channel created: #incident-IR-2026-0314.

Elaine (SRE): thanks all. closing the PagerDuty page for now. :white_check_mark:
